hook_text: Cooling towers on the horizon and a coal train a kilometre long. Inside, the same machine that runs on coal, gas, uranium or mirrors. Here is how it works and what each fuel costs.
clip_script: Heat boils water, steam spins a turbine, the turbine spins a magnet in coils, out goes alternating current through transformers. Forty percent becomes electricity; the rest warms the sky from the cooling towers, whose white plume is water, not smoke. Coal: ours, cheap, eighty percent of our power, and the dirtiest fuel there is, with an old fleet behind load shedding. Gas: half the carbon, starts in minutes, but imported in dollars. Nuclear: no smoke, tiny fuel, huge cost, waste for millennia. Solar thermal: mirrors, molten salt, free fuel into the evening. Compare them on the same list, and plan a just transition.
visual_style: Whiteboard station cutaway: boiler, turbine, generator, transformer; four fuel icons slot into the boiler in turn; a criteria table fills in; a cooling tower plume labelled water, a stack labelled smoke.
pacing: Machine, efficiency, coal, gas, nuclear, solar thermal, table.
